description: Audit how a dataset, survey, or study was collected and compared — not arithmetic, but whether the methodology supports the conclusion drawn. Checks five traps — survivorship, selection bias, confounding, measurement bias, self-selection/non-response — flagging only ones the setup actually creates, with the concrete mechanism, not a textbook definition. Built to NOT flag every bias reflexively: a sound study should come back clean. Use when the user pastes or describes a dataset, survey, study, or "the numbers show X" claim and wants a second opinion on whether the collection/comparison supports the conclusion; when they ask "is this study legit," "can I trust this survey," "what's wrong with this data," "is there a confound here," or "am I about to draw the wrong conclusion"; or before citing a stat they want checked first. Not for arithmetic, statistical significance, or factual accuracy of individual claims — only collection/comparison methodology.

results.query: This study only looked at successful companies — could that be skewing the conclusion?
